l: magic charm, The Emerald City of Oz, 29. How Glinda Worked a Magic Spell
s: Glinda possesses a magic charm powerful enough to make the Land of Oz invisible to all eyes but those of its inhabitants. She uses it to protect Oz from outsiders.

l: Magic Spell, The Emerald City of Oz, 29. How Glinda Worked a Magic Spell
s: The Magic Spell makes the Land of Oz invisible to people outside it. Glinda performs the spell before Ozma and the others arrive, leaving the inhabitants able to see Oz normally.

l: making Oz invisible, The Emerald City of Oz, 29. How Glinda Worked a Magic Spell
s: Making Oz invisible prevents people flying over it, approaching it from the desert, or tunneling toward it from seeing or finding the country. The change does not affect the inhabitants' ability to see one another or their land.

l: separation of Oz from the outside world, The Emerald City of Oz, 29. How Glinda Worked a Magic Spell
s: Ozma and Glinda decide that Oz should be separated from the outside world so that no one can communicate with it or travel there uninvited. Glinda's spell accomplishes this by hiding Oz from outsiders.

l: The Emerald City of Oz, The Emerald City of Oz, 30. How the Story of Oz Came to an End
s: The writer of these Oz stories receives a note from Princess Dorothy of Oz saying that Oz is cut off forever from the rest of the world. Dorothy says that she and Toto will always love the writer and the children who love them. Although the writer is initially saddened, he reflects that six story books have already told enough of the history of Oz. He wishes Dorothy and her companions a long and happy life in their invisible country.

l: Dorothy, The Emerald City of Oz, 30. How the Story of Oz Came to an End
s: Dorothy Gale sends the writer a note saying that Oz is now cut off forever from the rest of the world. She says that she and Toto will always love the writer and the other children who love them.

l: Toto, The Emerald City of Oz, 30. How the Story of Oz Came to an End
s: Toto is mentioned in Dorothy Gale's note as sharing her lasting love for the writer and the children who love them.

l: Oz, The Emerald City of Oz, 30. How the Story of Oz Came to an End
s: Oz becomes cut off forever from all the rest of the world and is described as an invisible country. The writer wishes Dorothy and her companions happiness there.

l: writer (of these Oz stories), The Emerald City of Oz, 30. How the Story of Oz Came to an End
s: The writer receives a note from Dorothy Gale written on a broad, white feather from a stork's wing, and the note makes him feel disconcerted for a time. He is initially saddened that he will hear no more about Oz, but he reflects on what has already been learned from its stories.

l: note (from Dorothy Gale), The Emerald City of Oz, 30. How the Story of Oz Came to an End
s: The note tells the writer that he will never hear anything more about Oz because the country is cut off forever from the rest of the world. It also says that Dorothy Gale and Toto will always love him and the children who love them.

l: Oz stories, The Emerald City of Oz, 30. How the Story of Oz Came to an End
s: The Oz stories have filled six story books. Through Oz's quaint people and strange adventures, they have provided many useful and amusing things to learn.

l: history of the Land of Oz, The Emerald City of Oz, 30. How the Story of Oz Came to an End
s: The history of the Land of Oz has been told across six story books. The writer considers this enough history to have been shared, despite being unable to hear more about Oz.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: TROT AND CAP'N BILL
s: Trot and Cap'n Bill sit beneath a giant acacia tree overlooking the Pacific Ocean and discuss mermaids. Cap'n Bill claims that anyone who sees a mermaid is lured into the water and drowns, though Trot points out that this account seems contradictory. He describes mermaids as beautiful, fish-tailed fairies with enchanting songs, and Trot says she would like to see one and survive. Their conversation ends when Trot's mother calls them into the house for supper.

l: Trot, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: TROT AND CAP'N BILL
s: Trot is a young girl who often sits with Cap'n Bill by the sea and listens to his stories. She questions his claims about mermaids, suggests that someone may have found a photograph of one, and says she would like to see a mermaid without being drowned.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: TROT AND CAP'N BILL
s: Cap'n Bill is an old sailor, formerly the owner and commander of the schooner Anemone, who now lives ashore with Trot's family after losing a leg. He tells Trot that mermaids are beautiful fairies who lure people into the water, but he struggles to explain how anyone knows what they look like if those who see them do not survive.

l: mermaids, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: TROT AND CAP'N BILL
s: Mermaids are described by Cap'n Bill as fairies that live deep in the water. They are said to sing sweet songs, smile and wink at people, and laugh when people drown.

l: Pacific Ocean, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: TROT AND CAP'N BILL
s: The Pacific Ocean rolls below the bluff where Trot and Cap'n Bill sit. Cap'n Bill and Trot often go to the tree at its edge to watch the ocean.

l: mermaid appearance and behavior, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: TROT AND CAP'N BILL
s: Cap'n Bill says mermaids have a lovely lady's form down to the waist and a fish's lower half covered with green, purple, and pink scales. He describes them as having arms, pretty faces, long silky hair that floats in the water, and sweet singing voices; he also says they charm people and cause them to plunge into the waves.

l: drowning by mermaids, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: TROT AND CAP'N BILL
s: Cap'n Bill claims that nobody who has seen a mermaid has lived to tell the tale because mermaids lure people into the water with their beauty and songs. He says that even people who know how to swim cannot escape because mermaids live deep down, and that the victims never come up again.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap 2._
s: Trot and Cap'n Bill take Trot's rowboat into Giant's Cave, where they discover a glowing blue underwater cavern. Mermaids appear around the boat and explain that they are water fairies who wish to please people and can transform visitors so they can live underwater. Trot accepts an invitation to visit the mermaids' deep-sea kingdom, and Cap'n Bill reluctantly follows to look after her. Trot takes Clia's hand, falls into the water, and calls cheerfully for Cap'n Bill to join her.

Trot rows with Cap'n Bill to Giant's Cave and eagerly explores the glowing cavern. She is delighted to meet the mermaids, accepts their invitation to visit their kingdom, takes Clia's hand, and enters the water after being changed to live beneath it.

Cap'n Bill rows Trot's boat into Giant's Cave and is frightened when the mermaids appear. Although he doubts their safety and worries about Trot, he agrees to follow her underwater so he can look after her.
Clia is a mermaid princess who invites Trot and Cap'n Bill to visit the mermaids' deep-sea kingdom. She offers Trot her hand and helps transform the visitors so they can live underwater.

The mermaids appear in Giant's Cave as beautiful, friendly water fairies. They say that they love little girls, can use magic to protect or transform visitors, and invite Trot and Cap'n Bill to see their underwater home.
Giant's Cave is an extensive, low-roofed cave beneath the coast, filled with deep water. Its interior glows sapphire blue, and its waves and spray shine like jewels.

The ocean is a beloved companion to Trot and Cap'n Bill, whether it is stormy, breaking against the shore, or calm. In Giant's Cave, it appears beneath the rock dome in a beautiful sapphire and azure form.

l: boat (Trot and Cap'n Bill's boat), The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap 2._
s: Trot's rowboat is lowered from its shelter on the cliff and pushed into the sea. Cap'n Bill rows it around the caves and into Giant's Cave, where it drifts while Trot and he admire the cavern.

l: the mermaids' deep-sea kingdom, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap 2._
s: The mermaids' deep-sea kingdom is an underwater realm containing wonders that Trot wants to see. The mermaids offer to take Trot and Cap'n Bill there and return them safely to Giant's Cave when they are ready.

l: Trot and Cap'n Bill's visit to the ocean palaces, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap 2._
s: Trot's visit to the mermaids begins when she accepts their invitation to explore their underwater home. Clia takes her hand, Trot enters the water without being hurt, and she excitedly urges Cap'n Bill to come along.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 3._
s: Cap'n Bill joins Trot and the mermaids in the water and discovers that he has become a merman with a powerful green-scaled tail. Princess Clia and Merla guide Cap'n Bill and Trot through the ocean, protecting them from possible dangers such as sharks and devilfish. The mermaids explain that sea serpents are ancient, harmless, and kind, and that the mermaid palaces lie hundreds of miles away in the deepest part of the ocean. Using fairy power, the group travels swiftly toward the palaces.

Cap'n Bill enters the water with Trot and finds himself comfortable despite his fear of rheumatism. He discovers that he can swim, dive, and move more skillfully than ever, and he learns that his green-scaled tail is more useful than his wooden leg. He is guided by Merla and remains wary of sharks, devilfish, and other dangers.

Trot swims with the mermaids and enjoys her new pink-scaled tail, which gleams like jewels. She can see clearly underwater and asks questions about the ocean's dangers, the sea serpents, and the ages of the mermaids. She travels trustfully beside Princess Clia toward the mermaid palaces.

Princess Clia helps Cap'n Bill enter the water and leads him and Trot through the ocean. She explains that mortals need protection from some sea creatures, describes the dangers of sharks and devilfish, and reveals that the sea serpents are harmless and kind. She uses fairy power to shorten the journey to the mermaid palaces.

Merla, a blonde mermaid and Princess Clia's cousin, guides Cap'n Bill by holding his hand so he will not lose the way. She promises to protect him during the journey and explains that the three sea serpents have gray whiskers and visit one another every hundred years.

The mermaids travel with Trot and Cap'n Bill through the ocean and protect the mortal travelers from harm. They wear flowing, transparent gowns decorated with pearls, and their hair floats freely around them. They are fairies who cannot be injured by anything in the ocean and are portrayed as joyful, playful, and long-lived.

The ocean contains dark caves, bright open waters, schools of fish, sharks, devilfish, and sea serpents. Its bottom is rugged and mountainous in places, while the mid-water allows faster travel but is less safe. The deepest part of the ocean is where the mermaid palaces are located.

The cave is the place where the journey begins. It temporarily blocks the light as the travelers descend through the water, and the group leaves it before swimming onward through brighter parts of the sea.

l: the mermaid palaces, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 3._
s: The mermaid palaces are the travelers' destination and are located at the very bottom of the ocean, in its deepest part. They are inhabited only by mermaids, so sharks cannot enter them.
Fairy power protects the mermaids from injury and allows them to guard mortal companions in the ocean. Princess Clia uses some of this power to help the group travel hundreds of miles without tiring.

l: Trot and Cap'n Bill's visit to the ocean palaces, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 3._
s: The journey begins when Princess Clia and Merla guide Trot and Cap'n Bill away from the cave and through mid-water. The travelers encounter schools of harmless yellowtail fish and learn to avoid sharks and devilfish. Fairy power speeds their progress, and they eventually begin descending toward the palaces in the deepest part of the ocean.

l: Cap'n Bill's transformation into a merman, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 3._
s: When Cap'n Bill takes Princess Clia's hand and enters the water, he becomes a merman with a green, emerald-like scaled tail. He can swim, dive, and perform movements far better than he could on land, while his clothing remains dry and warm. Princess Clia says that he will become ordinary Cap'n Bill again, wooden leg and all, when he returns home.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: The PALACE OF QUEEN AQUARINE
s: Trot and Cap'n Bill descend into the ocean with Princess Clia and the mermaids and discover that they can breathe, swim, and remain dry through magic. They pass through colorful gardens guarded by swordfishes and arrive at the mermaids' coral palaces, where Queen Aquareine welcomes them. Queen Aquareine shows them that Trot's mother is asleep under an enchantment and promises to protect the house while the visitors remain below the sea. The queen explains the magical air space around mermaids and visitors, the use of fins, and the nature of mirages.

l: Trot, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: The PALACE OF QUEEN AQUARINE
s: Trot descends into the ocean with Cap'n Bill and the mermaids, finding that the water supports her and that she can breathe without gills. She is astonished by the colorful sea gardens and the mermaids' palaces, welcomes Queen Aquareine's hospitality, and worries about her mother's safety while she is away.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: The PALACE OF QUEEN AQUARINE
s: Cap'n Bill descends into the ocean with Trot and observes that they can breathe and move without gills. He recalls that some swordfishes attack ships, is embarrassed by his former ideas about mermaids, and asks Queen Aquareine whether the dampness will worsen his rheumatics.

l: Princess Clia, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: The PALACE OF QUEEN AQUARINE
s: Princess Clia leads Trot and Cap'n Bill through the sea gardens and into the mermaids' palace. She explains that the swordfishes guard the garden entrances and welcomes the visitors to the palace.

l: Queen Aquareine, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: The PALACE OF QUEEN AQUARINE
s: Queen Aquareine welcomes Trot and Cap'n Bill and invites them to remain in the ocean palaces for several days. She uses magic to put Trot's mother into a pleasant sleep, protects the house, demonstrates a scene through a mirage, and explains how the visitors can breathe and remain dry underwater.

l: mermaids, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: The PALACE OF QUEEN AQUARINE
s: The mermaids accompany Trot and Cap'n Bill through the ocean, laugh at Trot's observation that they must be breathing by magic, and escort the visitors to the palaces. They are described as beautiful, jeweled, and dressed in gauzy robes, and they rest on coral couches because of their tails.

l: Pacific Ocean, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: The PALACE OF QUEEN AQUARINE
s: The ocean is clear but tinted green, and it makes Trot and Cap'n Bill feel light and buoyant as they descend. Its bottom is covered with white sand and supports colorful sea shrubs, flowers, gardens, and coral palaces.

l: the gardens surrounding the mermaids' palaces, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: The PALACE OF QUEEN AQUARINE
s: The gardens are dense groves of large, brightly colored sea shrubs with entwined branches, strange fruits, and avenues leading toward the palaces. Swordfishes guard their entrances and drive away creatures that try to enter uninvited.

l: the mermaid palaces, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: The PALACE OF QUEEN AQUARINE
s: The mermaids' palaces are extensive coral buildings made with white, pink, and yellow coral arranged in graceful designs. Their roofs are made of glass through Queen Aquareine's fairy powers, and archways serve as entrances.

l: Queen Aquareine's throne room, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: The PALACE OF QUEEN AQUARINE
s: Queen Aquareine's throne room is the most magnificent chamber in the ocean palaces, with coral walls inlaid with mother-of-pearl, polished shells, gem-patterned floors, and coral couches. Queen Aquareine reclines on a raised mother-of-pearl platform upon a couch covered with diamonds, rubies, emeralds, and pearls.

l: mirage, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: The PALACE OF QUEEN AQUARINE
s: A mirage allows Queen Aquareine to bring an earthly scene before the visitors. She uses it to show Trot and Cap'n Bill that Trot's mother is asleep in the cottage, and explains that such scenes may sometimes be reflected above the water for mortals to see.

l: the air space around mermaids and visitors, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: The PALACE OF QUEEN AQUARINE
s: A very small air space remains between the mermaids and visitors and the surrounding water, so the water does not touch their bodies or gowns. The air space is continually replenished from air contained in the water, allowing them to breathe freely and remain warm and dry.

l: Trot and Cap'n Bill's visit to the ocean palaces, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: The PALACE OF QUEEN AQUARINE
s: Trot and Cap'n Bill are invited to stay in the ocean palaces for several days as honored guests. During their visit they see the gardens, coral buildings, and Queen Aquareine's throne room and learn about the magic that makes underwater travel possible.

l: the mother's enchanted sleep, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: The PALACE OF QUEEN AQUARINE
s: Queen Aquareine sends Trot's mother into a deep sleep so she will not worry while Trot is away. The enchantment gives her pleasant dreams and protects the house from intrusion; the queen shows the sleeping mother through a mirage.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap 5._
s: Trot and Cap'n Bill meet King Anko, the ancient sea serpent who rules the ocean but not the mermaids. Queen Aquareine explains that Anko is friendly and that the visitors can understand the language of every sea inhabitant. Anko describes his immense age, extraordinary length, past pains, and two shorter brothers, then leaves to return home for dinner. Trot and Cap'n Bill realize afterward that he forgot to explain his third pain.

Mayre is identified by Queen Aquareine as the young girl among the earth people, though she is referred to as Trot in the encounter. She questions whether King Anko can talk and understand them, asks about his toothache and length, and is puzzled by his explanation of the kink in his tail.

Cap'n Bill meets King Anko and exchanges questions about their ages and health. He admits that Anko is older than he is, says he would not want to live for so many years, and later observes that Anko's memory may be failing because he forgot to describe his third pain.

Queen Aquareine welcomes King Anko and explains to Trot that the sea serpent is friendly, rules the ocean, and does not rule the mermaids. She introduces the earth people to him and has given them the power to understand every inhabitant of the sea.

King Anko enters the throne room through an opening in the coral and meets Mayre and Cap'n Bill. He is a gentle, ancient sea serpent who remembers several thousand years, was once measured at 7,482 feet, five inches and a quarter, and has suffered three pains, including a toothache and a kink in his tail caused by an octopus. He says he is proud of his age, rule, and length, then leaves to go home for dinner and invites the visitors to see him.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 6._
s: Queen Aquareine hosts Trot and Cap'n Bill in her underwater palace, where they rest, answer questions, and share a large midday dinner with the mermaids. Afterward, Merla leads them on an afternoon swim through the sea gardens and into the ocean to see jellyfish, singing barnacles, and snapping eels. Cap'n Bill discovers that he can light and smoke his pipe underwater because an air space surrounds them. The travelers encounter playful snapping eels but are not harmed.

Trot rests in Queen Aquareine's palace, answers questions about life on land, and enjoys the sea fruit and the queen's dinner. She follows Cap'n Bill's example by eating unfamiliar foods and is delighted by the meal. During the afternoon swim, she admires the jellyfish, dislikes the nonsensical songs of the barnacles, and is relieved when the snapping eels leave.

Cap'n Bill rests in the palace, answers questions about life on earth, and eats everything offered at the queen's dinner. He successfully lights and smokes his pipe underwater because of the air space around him. During the afternoon swim, he avoids an eel's snap, objects when the eels call him a polliwog, and says that the eels are not respectful.

Queen Aquareine welcomes Trot and Cap'n Bill, provides them with food and lodging, and asks them about life on earth. She invites them to her dinner and later sends them on an afternoon swim with Merla. Merla says that Queen Aquareine can stiffen the snapping eels when they misbehave.

Merla warns Cap'n Bill not to spoil his appetite, explains how the mermaids cook without fires, and leads Trot and Cap'n Bill on an afternoon swim. She identifies the jellyfish, singing barnacles, sea pig, and snapping eels they encounter. She orders the eels to stop threatening the visitors and warns that Queen Aquareine may punish them.

The mermaids host Trot and Cap'n Bill, question them about human life, and share sea fruit and a formal dinner with them. They recline on couches while eating, and their palaces have separate tables for other mermaids. They use sunlight or hot springs for cooking and employ lobsters as slaves to serve meals.

l: the Palace of Queen Aquarine, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 6._
s: Queen Aquareine's palace contains couches, spacious rooms, a glass-roofed kitchen, hot springs, and flower gardens. Its curved kitchen roof concentrates sunlight strongly enough to cook food, while the hot springs provide heat on cloudy days. The palace is surrounded by dense shrubbery and has avenues leading from its sea garden into the ocean.

The ocean contains the mermaids' palaces and gardens, as well as jellyfish, singing barnacles, swordfish guards, sea pigs, and snapping eels. Ice for the mermaids' ice cream is brought from icebergs in the northern parts of the ocean. Trot and Cap'n Bill swim through the ocean during their afternoon excursion.

l: the queen's dinner, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 6._
s: The queen's dinner is served at noon to Queen Aquareine's nobility, favorites, and guests. It includes turtle soup, salmon steaks, fungus bread, oysters, clams, soft-shell crabs, seaweed salad, fruits, and flower-shaped ice creams. Large lobsters serve the courses backward and fussily, while the ice cream is made with ice brought from northern icebergs.

The jellyfish are a rare variety that float in the clear water and resemble inverted flowerpots with fluted edges. They are soft, transparent, and tinted sapphire blue, rose pink, or topaz, with flower-like forms floating from their centers. They have no apparent heads, eyes, or ears, live for a long time, and may be washed ashore if they get too near the surface.

l: the singing barnacles, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 6._
s: The singing barnacles cling to the steep surface of a large rock and produce a chorus of many small voices. Their songs concern ships, anchors, sea creatures, and other subjects but usually mean nothing because the barnacles have few brains. They sing all day and do not care whether their songs make sense.

l: the snapping eels, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 6._
s: The snapping eels wriggle and dart around Trot and Cap'n Bill, snapping near their fingers, noses, and faces. Merla orders them to stop and warns that Queen Aquareine can stiffen them for hurting earth people. The eels claim they will not harm the visitors, then swim away to frighten Mummercubble.

l: the afternoon swim, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 6._
s: The afternoon swim takes Trot and Cap'n Bill from Queen Aquareine's palace through the sea gardens and shrubbery into the ocean. Merla shows them jellyfish, singing barnacles, swordfish guards, and snapping eels. The excursion ends with the travelers left safely on their own after the eels dart away.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 7._
s: Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Merla explore the sea and visit codfish, Crabville, several kinds of crabs, mackerel, and balloonfish. The codfish are described as haughty, while the fiddler crabs play unpleasant music, the clown crabs perform repeated tricks, and the hermit crabs hide in shells and act unsociably. A mackerel named Flippity is caught by a hook, which the other mackerel mistakenly believe has taken him to glory. Merla explains various aspects of sea life, including why fish are caught and eaten, before leading Trot and Cap'n Bill back to the palace.

Trot explores the sea with Cap'n Bill and Merla, meeting codfish, fiddler crabs, clown crabs, hermit crabs, mackerel, and balloonfish. She insults the proud codfish, enjoys the clown crabs' antics, warns the mackerel that Flippity will be fried for someone's dinner, and questions why fish bite hooks.
Cap'n Bill explores the sea with Trot and Merla. He comments on codfish aristocracy, recognizes why people are called crabbed, and explains how balloonfish skins can be made into lanterns.

Merla guides Trot and Cap'n Bill through the sea, identifying the creatures they encounter and explaining their behavior. She describes codfish as aristocratic, the crabs as varied in nature, and the mackerel's belief that being caught means going to glory. She leads the travelers back to the palace before dark.
Mermaids have warned the fish that hooks bring death rather than happiness, but the fish do not heed the warnings. The mackerel regard Merla as someone who can explain what happens in the sea.

The codfish are described as dark-backed, silver underneath, and the most aristocratic family of fish in the sea. They are haughty and proud of their pedigree, take offense at being discussed by mermaids, and leave after Trot insults them.
Crabville is a place near a kelp bed where many families or varieties of crabs live. Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Merla visit it and see fiddler crabs, clown crabs, and hermit crabs.
The crabs live among rocks and kelp in Crabville and display many different behaviors. Some serve as household servants for mermaids, while others perform music, jokes, acrobatics, or hide in shells.

The fiddler crabs gather with fiddles and perform a composition called Number 19, 'Hail to the Mermaids.' Their music is shrill and unmusical to Trot and Cap'n Bill, though their leader calls it highly classical.

The clown crabs perform comic antics such as building pyramids, chasing one another, playing leapfrog, swinging on seaweed, and turning cartwheels. Tommy Blimken and Harry Hustle know about automobiles and life on land because humans once kept them in an aquarium before they escaped.
The hermit crabs live inside stolen conch shells to protect themselves from enemies. They are described as cowardly, cross, unsociable, and unwilling to have mermaids nearby.
The mackerel become excited when one of their group is caught by a hook and pulled from the water. They mistakenly believe that a fish taken by a hook has gone to a beautiful place called glory.

Flippity is a mackerel who eats bait on a spinning, shining hook and is pulled out of the water into a boat. Merla calls him the prettiest and nicest mackerel in his flock, while Trot explains that he will be fried for someone's dinner.

l: Flippity's going to glory, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 7._
s: Flippity's going to glory is the mackerel's mistaken description of his being caught by a hook and removed from the water. The other mackerel view it as splendid, not understanding that Flippity has died and will become food.

The sea contains deep water, kelp beds, rocky canyons, groves, palaces, and many kinds of fish and crabs. Trot and Cap'n Bill enjoy seeing its creatures in their natural surroundings, and the sea grows dark as the sun sets.

The earth is the dry, airy place where Trot and Cap'n Bill came from and where humans, horses, automobiles, and other creatures with legs live. Harry Hustle says he nearly died there because it was stupid, dry, and airy, although he enjoyed seeing a circus.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 8._
s: Trot and Cap'n Bill are welcomed to the mermaid palaces, where they are given rooms, dressed for the occasion, and served a lavish meal. They attend an underwater reception with mermaid music and dancing before sleeping in comfortable sponge-covered couches. The next morning, Queen Aquareine announces that she will take them to the ocean's most interesting regions to see the largest sea creatures and visit King Anko. Before they leave, she protects both guests with the Magic Circle.

Trot is amazed by the mermaid palaces and delighted with her beautiful room, gossamer gown, pearls, and comfortable couch. She enjoys the banquet and entertainment, sleeps soundly, and agrees eagerly to visit the largest sea creatures and King Anko. She receives the Magic Circle from Queen Aquareine before the journey.

Cap'n Bill is given a room near Trot's but refuses to change his clothes. He wonders why the deep water does not crush them and accepts Trot's explanation that magic keeps the water away from their bodies. After enjoying the banquet and entertainment, he receives the Magic Circle before leaving on the underwater journey.

Queen Aquareine welcomes Trot and Cap'n Bill and orders a banquet and entertainment for them. She plans to take them to the largest and most remarkable sea creatures and to visit King Anko. She draws the Magic Circle around both guests and leaves Merla to rule the palaces while she travels with them.

The mermaids guide Trot to her room, help her dress and arrange her hair, serve the guests, and entertain them with harp music, songs, and swimming-dances. They are described as fresh, lovely, sweet-tempered, and merry.

l: the mermaid palaces, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 8._
s: The mermaid palaces are brightly lit by electric jellyfish and contain rooms decorated with iridescent shells, coral furniture, amber sponges, and polished tortoise-shell conveniences. Their glass ceilings allow fishes and other sea creatures to look inside.

The ocean contains the mermaid palaces, sea gardens, phosphorescent creatures, and many remarkable and dangerous beings. Its deep water would press against and potentially crush unprotected bodies, but magic keeps it from touching Trot and Cap'n Bill.
Electric jellyfish naturally emit strong, beautiful electric light. The mermaids keep hundreds of them in their palaces, where they are clustered on ceilings and illuminate the rooms like daylight.

l: Fairy Circle of Queen Aquareine, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 8._
s: The Magic Circle is a fairy charm that prevents enemies from touching the person it protects. Queen Aquareine creates it by swimming around Trot and Cap'n Bill in opposite-direction circles with her wand.

l: the royal banquet, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 8._
s: The royal banquet is served to Trot and Cap'n Bill in Queen Aquareine's hall. It consists of many delicious courses, although a lobster accidentally spills hot soup on Cap'n Bill's bald head.

l: the largest sea creatures, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 8._
s: The largest and most remarkable sea creatures live in a part of the ocean that Queen Aquareine plans to visit with Trot and Cap'n Bill. Some nearby beings are fierce and terrible and would attack the guests if they knew they were earth people.

l: the underwater journey, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 8._
s: The underwater journey begins after breakfast when Queen Aquareine, Princess Clia, Trot, and Cap'n Bill leave the mermaid palace. They plan to travel to the region where the largest sea creatures live and to visit King Anko, with the guests protected by the Magic Circle.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 9._
s: Queen Aquareine, Princess Clia, Trot, and Cap'n Bill swim through the sea to visit unusual creatures and plants. They meet a bashful octopus, who is distressed that humans compare octopuses to wicked and deceitful organizations. The party is attacked unsuccessfully by sawfishes because the Magic Circle protects them, then descends into darker waters and observes phosphorescent fish and argonauts. Queen Aquareine also explains the danger posed by sea devils and the imprisoned magician Zog, who fears King Anko.

Queen Aquareine leads Princess Clia, Trot, and Cap'n Bill through the open sea to see unusual sea creatures and plants. She explains the nature of octopuses, sea devils, Zog, King Anko, sawfishes, and the Magic Circle, and urges the group to stay together.

Princess Clia travels with Queen Aquareine, Trot, and Cap'n Bill. She warns Trot that the creature approaching them is an octopus and explains that octopi are not very bad, though their cousins the sea devils are feared.

Trot meets a well-dressed octopus and argues with him over the names octopus and octopi, calling octopuses horrid, horrible, wicked, and deceitful. She is briefly frightened by the sawfishes but is delighted when the Magic Circle protects the group, and she later watches the argonauts with curiosity.

Cap'n Bill accompanies Queen Aquareine, Princess Clia, and Trot on their exploration. He agrees that scientists gave creatures difficult names, supports Trot's negative opinion of the octopus, asks about sea devils and Zog, and witnesses the failed sawfish attack.
The mermaids travel through the sea with Trot and Cap'n Bill. Butterfly fish greet them, and the octopus addresses them as neighbors.

The sea is clear and bright near the surface, with water that looks azure under the sun. It grows darker blue as the party descends, where some fish produce their own phosphorescent light and Zog is said to have been cast from the earth into the sea.

l: octopus (the bashful octopus), The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 9._
s: The octopus approaches the party wearing a red coat, brass buttons, a silk hat, and a yellow embroidered vest, while using some of his legs as arms. He is offended and deeply ashamed when Trot and Cap'n Bill say that people on earth compare octopuses to the Stannerd Oil Company and the Coal Trust, and he weeps as the party leaves.

The sea devils are described as much larger than an octopus, bright scarlet with black stripes, fierce, and terrible. They are the only ocean creatures the mermaids greatly fear, and they live near the dismal caverns.

Zog is described as the wicked genius of the sea and a powerful magician who is part fish, part man, part beast, and part serpent. King Anko defeated him and drove him into an invisible enchanted castle, where he has remained shut up and has not dared to do an evil deed for many years.
King Anko is the sea serpent who conquered Zog and drove him into his enchanted castle. He would kill Zog if he caught him outside the castle, and Zog knows this.

An army of sawfishes attacks the party with long saws covered in sharp hooked teeth. The sawfishes cannot touch anyone because the Magic Circle turns their saws aside, so they abandon the attack and swim away in disappointment.

l: Fairy Circle of Queen Aquareine, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 9._
s: The Magic Circle protects Queen Aquareine, Princess Clia, Trot, and Cap'n Bill from the sawfishes. It is powerful enough to turn aside the fishes' ugly saws and prevent them from disturbing the party.

l: the fleet of argonauts, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 9._
s: The party encounters a school of argonauts traveling toward the surface for a sail. Argonauts live in shells, hide in them from wolf fishes, carry the shells like humps, and spread skinny sails to travel through the water and later float on air currents at the surface.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 10._
s: Trot, Cap'n Bill, Queen Aquareine, and Clia travel through the ocean and discover an unnamed island that has never been seen by humans. Beneath the water, they observe colorful weeds, starfishes, sea horses, and sea spiders before reaching the island's surface. The island is inhabited by seals and turtles and visited by sea-gulls. Chief Muffruff's teasing of a turtle leads to a quarrel in which the turtles drive the seals from the island.

Trot travels with Cap'n Bill, Queen Aquareine, and Clia through the ocean. She observes starfishes and sea horses, speaks with a sea horse, dislikes the sea spiders, and is astonished to reach the surface near the undiscovered island. She laughs at the quarrel between the seals and turtles.

Cap'n Bill accompanies Trot, Queen Aquareine, and Clia through the ocean. He asks what island they are near and what the sea-gulls find to eat, and he is introduced to Chief Muffruff as an earth dweller and sailor.

Queen Aquareine guides Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Clia upward through the ocean to an unnamed island. She explains the habits of starfishes, sea horses, turtles, seals, and sea-gulls, and recognizes Chief Muffruff. After the turtles defeat the seals, she leads the group back beneath the water.
The mermaids travel with Trot and Cap'n Bill near the undiscovered island. The seals can swim more quickly than sea horses, but the sea horses cannot swim as the mermaids do.

l: the undiscovered island, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 10._
s: The island has no name because it has never been discovered or inhabited by humans. It is a barren, rocky islet with no trees, bushes, or grass, and it is inhabited by seals and turtles, with sea-gulls nesting on its central cliffs.

The ocean contains open sandy spaces covered sparsely with brilliantly colored weeds and inhabited by starfishes, sea horses, and sea spiders. Trot and her companions rise through it to the surface near the undiscovered island, then return beneath the water.

Hundreds of starfishes lie on the sandy ocean floor in various colors, usually motionless with their points extended. Some wind their arms around weeds or use their points as legs, and one claims to be over three months old.

The small sea horses live among the ocean weeds and support themselves by twining their tails around the stems. Their side fins also serve as ears, they have small fins on their backs, and they swim less swiftly than mermaids and fishes. They face danger from fishes and other living things, though one has survived for over six weeks.

Many seals live on the rocky island, where they sleep, sun themselves, crawl about, and bark. The young seals are active and playful, and seals feed on sea-gulls and their eggs. They quarrel with the turtles and are driven into the water after the turtles attack them.

Chief Muffruff is the chief of the disorderly family of seals living on and around the island. He recognizes Queen Aquareine and Clia, jokes about Cap'n Bill being bald-headed, and starts a quarrel by flipping a turtle onto its back. The turtles bite his fins and tail before he escapes into the water.

Many turtles rest at the edge of the water, including some as large as wagon wheels and possibly hundreds of years old. One turtle objects to Muffruff's treatment of it, and the turtles later rush the seals, bite Chief Muffruff, and take undisputed possession of the island.

l: the seals-versus-turtles quarrels, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 10._
s: The quarrels between the seals and turtles are frequent but usually temporary. In this incident, Chief Muffruff flips a turtle onto its back, the young seals push it into the water, and the turtles retaliate by driving the seals away and biting Muffruff. Queen Aquareine says the animals will probably be sleeping together again within an hour.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 11._
s: Trot, Cap'n Bill, Queen Aquareine, and Princess Clia are driven through the ocean by cuttlefish ink toward the Devil Caves and the hidden castle of Zog the Terrible. Sea devils surround them, using their crimson feelers to form a cage that carries the group forward. The mermaids' fairy circles prevent the sea devils from touching them, but the group is nevertheless trapped and unable to escape.

Trot travels with Cap'n Bill, Queen Aquareine, and Princess Clia through the ocean depths. She sees the sea devils surrounding them, remains comparatively calm, and correctly realizes that the cage is moving.
Cap'n Bill becomes disturbed by the cuttlefish ink and the sea devils, muttering and growling to himself. He travels with the others into the cage formed by the sea devils.

Queen Aquareine recognizes that the cuttlefish are driving the group toward the Devil Caves and tries to retreat, but the ink blocks their escape. She stops the group rather than letting it be driven farther and declares that the sea devils cannot harm them because of the protecting magic circles.

Princess Clia explains how cuttlefish carry and release their ink, warns Trot not to look up, and stays close to protect her. She insists that the fairy circles have foiled their enemies before, but she is trapped with the others when the sea devils form their cage.
Zog the Terrible is identified as the master whom the sea devils serve. Queen Aquareine believes the group may be near his hidden castle.

The sea devils use cuttlefish to drive the group toward the Devil Caves. They surround the travelers, laugh at the fairy circles, and interlace their long feelers to form a cage that carries the prisoners forward.
The cuttlefish release large clouds of ink to darken the water and hide themselves. They are servants of the sea devils and use the ink to force the group toward the Devil Caves.
The ocean depths become dark when cuttlefish ink spreads through the water. The travelers are forced to move through the only clear passage while the sea devils' cage carries them forward.

l: the Devil Caves, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 11._
s: The Devil Caves are a dangerous destination that Queen Aquareine initially wishes to avoid. The cuttlefish and sea devils drive the group toward them.

l: Fairy Circle of Queen Aquareine, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 11._
s: The fairy circles protect Trot, Cap'n Bill, Queen Aquareine, and Princess Clia from physical contact with the sea devils. The sea devils claim to know about the circles and say they do not think much of them.
Cuttlefish ink spreads through large areas of the water, making it nearly black. The ink blocks the group's routes and repeatedly drives it toward the sea devils' chosen direction.

l: the cage formed by the sea devils, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 11._
s: The cage formed by the sea devils is made by interlacing their long arms or feelers around the travelers. It has no opening large enough for escape and carries its prisoners forward as the sea devils swim.

l: Zog's capture of the prisoners, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 11._
s: The sea-devil capture begins when the monsters surround the group from above, behind, and both sides. Although the protecting magic circles keep the captors from touching them, the travelers are enclosed, carried away, and unable to escape.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 12._
s: Trot, Cap'n Bill, Queen Aquareine, and Princess Clia escape the sea devils and enter a silver passage leading to a vast sea cavern and the Palace of Zog. Aquareine suspects they are in the hidden dominions of Zog and decides to face the magician rather than retreat. At the palace they meet Prince Sacho of Sacharhineolaland, now a slave, who leads them through the castle and a magical maze to Zog's presence. The group passes through an illusory wall into a magnificent chamber.

Trot escapes the sea devils with Cap'n Bill, Queen Aquareine, and Princess Clia, but becomes worried about being far from her home and mother. She is less afraid than expected and relies more on Cap'n Bill than on her newer companions. At the Palace of Zog, she questions Sacho and protests when a magical barrier appears to block their way.

Cap'n Bill escapes the sea-devil cage with the others but remains deeply worried about Trot's safety. He doubts that Queen Aquareine can defeat Zog and finds the palace maze bewildering. He follows Clia through the maze while holding her hand.

Queen Aquareine leads the group out of the sea-devil enclosure and identifies their passage as possibly belonging to the hidden dominions of Zog. She chooses to face Zog rather than turn back and relies on her fairy powers to protect her companions. She recognizes the magical illusion concealing the chamber entrance and swims through it.

Princess Clia escapes with the group and reassures Cap'n Bill that Trot's end is not near. She says that she or Queen Aquareine could guide the others safely back through the maze. She leads Cap'n Bill by the hand as they follow Sacho.

Zog the Forsaken is described as a fearful magician who hates all the world and is hated by all the world. He commands the group to appear before him and is said to become dangerous when he smiles. He rules a castle beneath the sea and keeps numerous slaves in his domain.

Prince Sacho of Sacharhineolaland is now known in Zog's domain only as a slave. After surviving a shipwreck, he was saved by Zog, magically adapted to live underwater, and taught to serve in the castle. He receives the group, warns them about Zog, and guides them through the castle and maze.

The sea devils trap Trot, Cap'n Bill, Queen Aquareine, and Princess Clia in a cage of scarlet arms. They allow the cage to open but laugh harshly as the group escapes, warning that the escape has not yet fully succeeded. They do not follow into the silver passage.

The mermaids possess fairy powers and have a queen named Aquareine. Aquareine says that the mermaids have never before measured their strength against Zog, though she believes she may be able to defeat him if King Anko could do so.

l: the hidden dominions of Zog, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 12._
s: The hidden dominions of Zog are identified as the only place where the silver passage could exist without Queen Aquareine's knowledge. They contain a vast sea cavern, a coral-and-silver castle, and numerous slaves.

The Palace of Zog stands in the center of a vast sea cavern and is built of coral inlaid with silver, with clear glass windows. Its interior resembles an earthly castle, with halls, stairs, balconies, chairs, benches, curtained doorways, and magical passages. Strange many-eyed, quilled fish guard the entrance.

l: the cavern beneath the sea-devil's rock, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 12._
s: The sea cavern is enormous, with a dome resembling the sky viewed from earth. It contains Zog's coral castle, carefully arranged beds of sea flowers, and goldfish and silverfish moving among the foliage.

The maze inside Zog's domain has frequent twists, turns, sharp corners, crossings, and passages that vary from wide to extremely narrow. Its polished marble walls have no visible marks, but Sacho navigates it without hesitation. Clia says that she or Aquareine could lead the group safely back through it.

Zog's magic enables Sacho to live underwater like a fish and makes the maze's apparent barriers deceptive. Under its influence, a solid-looking marble wall melts away when the group swims toward it, revealing a splendid chamber.

l: slavery in Zog's domain, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 12._
s: Zog's domain contains dozens or possibly hundreds of slaves, all serving Zog as their only master. Sacho says there is no jealousy among them because they belong to the same class, and he is commanded to hate Zog even though he does not personally hate him.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 13._
s: Zog explains that he captured Queen Aquareine, Princess Clia, Trot, and Cap'n Bill to destroy them as revenge against King Anko, whom he hates. He says the prisoners will remain in his enchanted castle while he experiments with ways to overcome the mermaids' fairy power and destroy them. Zog assigns the mermaids and Trot to the Rose Chamber and Cap'n Bill to the Peony Room, allowing them to roam the castle but not leave it. Sacho guides them to their rooms and offers to help with their comfort.
Zog is a wicked magician and sea monster who lives in an enchanted castle. He admits that he captured the prisoners to destroy friends of King Anko, and he claims that only Anko can destroy him.
Queen Aquareine confronts Zog and challenges his power to destroy the mermaids. Zog identifies her as the first mermaid ever created and says she is his prisoner in the castle.
Trot tells Zog that he is hateful and disgusting, but she remains cheerful and refuses to leave Cap'n Bill behind. She is assigned to live in the Rose Chamber with the mermaids.
Cap'n Bill insults Zog and offers to die in Trot's place if Zog will send her safely home, but Trot rejects the proposal. He is assigned to live in the Peony Room.
Princess Clia asks why Zog seeks revenge against the prisoners even though they have never harmed him. She is taken with Queen Aquareine and Trot to the Rose Chamber.
King Anko is a sea serpent and Zog's great enemy. Zog says that Anko is the only being able to destroy him, but he has spent thousands of years trying to find a way to destroy Anko himself.

Sacho is a boy who serves Zog and escorts the prisoners through the castle. He shows them the Rose Chamber and Peony Room, explains that they may roam the castle but cannot leave, and offers to look after their comfort.
The mermaids are friends of King Anko whom Zog has captured for revenge. They claim that none of their race has ever died or been destroyed, and Zog intends to experiment on them.
The sea devils are the only sea dwellers permitted to serve Zog. Acting on his command, they surrounded and tricked the prisoners into reaching the entrance of his enchanted castle.

l: the prisoners' rooms, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 13._
s: The prisoners are Queen Aquareine, Princess Clia, Trot, and Cap'n Bill. They are held in Zog's castle, may roam within it, and cannot escape because the outer passages are guarded.
The enchanted castle is Zog's underwater domain, where his power is supreme. Its passages are guarded, but Zog permits the prisoners to move throughout the castle while remaining unable to leave.

l: the golden dome room, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 13._
s: The golden dome room is Zog's richly decorated den, made of solid gold and set with jewels and pearls. Zog interrogates and threatens the prisoners there before sending them to separate rooms.

l: the Rose Chamber, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 13._
s: The Rose Chamber is the room where Zog orders Queen Aquareine, Princess Clia, and Trot to live until they die. Its entrance is marked by roses sewn in pearls on the seaweed hangings.

l: the Peony Room, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 13._
s: The Peony Room is assigned to Cap'n Bill as his place of confinement. It is the room next to the Rose Chamber.
Zog says he will use his magic to test and overcome the mermaids. He claims his power is supreme within the enchanted castle.
The prisoners' fairy power is to be tested against Zog's magic. Zog plans to wear it down gradually.
Zog's vengeance is directed at King Anko, whom he hates but cannot directly hurt. He intends to make Anko suffer by destroying Anko's friends.

l: the prisoners' destruction, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 13._
s: The prisoners' destruction is Zog's stated purpose in capturing them. He plans to delay their deaths so that he can enjoy their despair and struggles.

l: Zog's capture of the prisoners, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 13._
s: Zog's sea devils captured the prisoners after his spies warned him that they had left Queen Aquareine's palace. They surrounded the group and forced them to the entrance of the enchanted castle.
Zog says that death itself is not as painful to mortals as the fear and anticipation before it. Cap'n Bill offers to die, even twice or three times, if Trot can be sent safely home.

l: the mermaids' immortality, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 13._
s: The mermaids claim that no mermaid has ever died or been destroyed. Zog says that Queen Aquareine, whom he identifies as the first mermaid, is still living.

l: Zog's hatred of Anko, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 13._
s: Zog has hated King Anko for thousands of years and refuses to let Anko kill him, even though Anko alone has the power to destroy him. He has spent three thousand six hundred and forty-two years, eleven months, and nine days seeking a way to destroy Anko.

l: the prisoners' confinement, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 13._
s: Zog orders the prisoners to remain in the enchanted castle until he can stop them from living. They may wander inside the castle, but its guarded outer passages prevent them from leaving.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 14._
s: Cap'n Bill and Trot explore their rooms in Zog's enchanted castle, where they discover that Cap'n Bill's quarters contain a seemingly identical wooden-legged sailor. The sailor is Cap'n Joe Weedles, Cap'n Bill's long-lost brother, whom Zog transformed with gills after rescuing him from a wreck. Cap'n Joe explains that he serves Zog by sewing buttons onto the magician's clothes and warns that escaping Zog will be extremely difficult. He says Sacho may be able to help the prisoners, while Trot and Cap'n Bill discuss Joe's life beneath the sea.

Zog provided handsome rooms for his prisoners and had furnished them with treasures taken from sunken ships. He transformed Cap'n Joe Weedles by giving him gills, keeps many slaves in his castle, and is described as cruel, grumbling, and nearly devilish.

Cap'n Bill explores the Peony Room and is startled when a supposed reflection turns out to be his long-lost brother, Cap'n Joe Weedles. He learns that Joe was transformed into a water-breathing servant of Zog and worries about the difficulty of escaping the castle.

Trot visits Cap'n Bill in the Peony Room and helps him realize that the wooden-legged sailor is not his reflection. She asks Cap'n Joe about Zog and escape, laughs at Joe's awkward movements, and learns that Sacho may be able to help them.

Cap'n Joe Weedles is Cap'n Bill's long-lost brother and a former sailor of the brig Gladsome. Zog gave him gills after finding him following a shipwreck, and Joe now lives underwater as a slave who sews buttons onto Zog's clothes. He says the work is easy and the rations are fair, but warns that Zog has never allowed anyone to escape.

The mermaids occupy the Rose Chamber, which contains golden rose decorations and couches made with mother-of-pearl frames and soft white sponges. They examine and admire the room while staying as prisoners in Zog's castle.

Zog's enchanted castle contains lavish rooms decorated with gold, mirrors, unusual furniture, and objects plundered from sunken ships. It lies fifty fathoms beneath the sea and houses Zog's prisoners and many slaves, who are not normally allowed to leave the great cave.

Zog's magic surrounds the castle and prevents the slaves from leaving the great cave. It also enabled Zog to give Cap'n Joe gills so he could live underwater, though Joe can no longer breathe air on land.

l: escape from Zog's castle, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 14._
s: Cap'n Joe does not know how to help the prisoners escape because magic surrounds the castle and no slave has escaped Zog. He suggests that Sacho, who knows a great deal, may be able to help them.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 15._
s: Trot, Cap'n Bill, Queen Aquareine, and Princess Clia are held captive in Zog's castle and discuss escaping through an opening in its dome. Chief cook Tom Atto provides them with a meal, while Zog's slaves appear cheerful despite their servitude. Zog subjects the four captives to a first trial of strength by setting the Yell-Maker upon them, but Queen Aquareine's magic protects them. Aquareine destroys the Yell-Maker, and Zog then causes the marble ceiling to collapse over the captives, without harming them.

Trot eats heartily after telling Tom Atto that she is hungry and helps plan an escape from Zog's castle. She is protected from the Yell-Maker's claws by the Fairy Circle of Queen Aquareine and remains unharmed when the marble ceiling collapses.
Cap'n Bill eats with the others and discusses ways to escape from Zog's castle. The Yell-Maker cannot hurt him, and he remains unharmed when Zog causes marble blocks to fall from the ceiling.

Queen Aquareine gives Tom Atto a ring that keeps prepared food from becoming wet and considers escaping through an opening in the castle's dome. Her magic protects the captives from the Yell-Maker and the falling marble, and she destroys the Yell-Maker with her fairy wand.

Princess Clia notices a possible opening at the top of the castle's dome and helps the others consider escaping through it. She is unharmed by the Yell-Maker and by the collapse of the marble ceiling.

Zog summons the captives to undergo a first trial of strength and orders the Yell-Maker to make them yell. He watches as Queen Aquareine destroys the creature, then causes the marble ceiling to collapse over the captives, but neither attack harms them.

The Yell-Maker is a black, crab-like sea creature with six long hinged legs ending in powerful claws. It repeatedly tries to pinch the four captives but cannot touch them, and Queen Aquareine's wand turns it into a pulpy mass that melts away forever.

Queen Aquareine identifies herself as the ruler of the mermaids, and Princess Clia is identified as a mermaid princess. The mermaids keep their belongings dry by surrounding them with air, unlike those living under the water in Zog's castle.

Zog's slaves include men, women, and children who wear gold bands around their ankles and have gills for breathing underwater. They appear jolly and serene rather than miserable, but they tremble whenever Zog smiles.

Zog's castle is enclosed under a great dome and contains confined water kept fresh by air fountains. It has a large central chamber, guarded outlets, and a possible opening in the dome through which the captives hope to escape.

The captives hope to return to the broad ocean by breaking through a castle window and swimming upward through the opening in the dome. Queen Aquareine destroys the Yell-Maker so that it disappears forever from the ocean.

l: Fairy Circle of Queen Aquareine, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 15._
s: The Fairy Circle of Queen Aquareine keeps Queen Aquareine, Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Princess Clia safe from the Yell-Maker's attacks. It also prevents the falling marble from touching them.

Queen Aquareine believes her fairy powers may be stronger than the evil magic controlled by Zog. Her magic protects the captives, while her fairy wand destroys the Yell-Maker; Zog claims that he learned the same kind of destructive trick thousands of years earlier.

l: escape from Zog's castle, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 15._
s: The captives consider breaking a window and swimming upward to an opening in the dome, which they think would lead back to the ocean more quickly than the winding passages. Queen Aquareine advises waiting for a time when they are not closely watched.

l: first trial of strength, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 15._
s: Zog declares that the captives have been brought before him for the first trial of strength between them. He tests them with the Yell-Maker, but the creature is powerless against them.
The Yell-Maker attacks Queen Aquareine, Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Princess Clia with its long legs and snapping claws. The Fairy Circle protects all four, so none is touched or made to yell.

l: destruction of the Yell-Maker, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 15._
s: Queen Aquareine calls the Yell-Maker an evil thing and waves her fairy wand at it. The creature becomes unconscious, its legs and claws fall apart, and its body withers into a pulpy mass before melting away forever.

l: marble ceiling collapse, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 15._
s: Zog causes the marble blocks above the captives to break loose and crash down in an attempt to crush them. The captives remain unharmed because the marble cannot touch them and is diverted from its course.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 16._
s: Zog abandons his attempt to crush Cap'n Bill, Trot, Aquareine, and Clia with marble blocks and sends them back to their rooms, while Sacho warns that Zog may be planning to kill them. Aquareine decides they must try to escape, but learns that the great dome's opening is guarded by the prince of the sea devils and that every entrance is watched. The prisoners discover that Zog's enchanted castle has constant magical light, with no day or night, and that Zog supposedly has not slept for hundreds of years. Unable to escape immediately, they eat a fine dinner and sleep while preparing for a future attempt.

Cap'n Bill's heart beats fast during Zog's marble-block threat, though he does not show his fear. He doubts their chances against Zog and hopes they will not have to fight the sea devils, but later eats dinner and sleeps in the Peony Room.
Trot remains confident in the protection of the fairy mermaids and calls Zog wicked. She encourages Cap'n Bill to trust Aquareine and later eats dinner and sleeps with the others.

Aquareine stays calm during Zog's attack and questions Sacho about guarded exits. She concludes that Zog will try more powerful attacks and plans for the group to escape, but learns that there is no night and that Zog never sleeps.
Clia remains calm after Zog's threat and asks Sacho whether he will help them escape. She also asks what causes the constant light in the castle.

Zog stops the marble-block attack, threatens the prisoners, and sends them back to their rooms. He is said to be plotting to kill them, to guard every entrance, and to have kept the castle's light shining continuously; Sacho says Zog has not slept for hundreds of years.

Sacho leads the prisoners back to their rooms and tells them that Zog has no time for vengeance but may be planning to kill them. He explains that the great dome's opening and all other entrances are guarded, and refuses to leave because he is happy among his fellow slaves.
The fairy mermaids are trusted by Trot to protect the group from danger.
The sea devils guard the great dome's opening and are described as a race with curling legs. Their prince is the largest and fiercest of them.

l: the prince of the sea devils, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 16._
s: The prince of the sea devils lies crouched over the opening in the great dome day and night. He is the largest and fiercest of his race and prevents anyone from passing his network of curling legs.
The enchanted castle stands in a large cave beneath the ocean. No one in the ocean can see it unless Zog wishes, and its entrances are kept guarded.

l: the cavern beneath the sea-devil's rock, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 16._
s: The great dome surrounds the castle and has an opening that is guarded by the prince of the sea devils. Its brilliant light does not fade, even after several hours.

l: escape from Zog's castle, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 16._
s: Aquareine decides that the group must attempt to escape before Zog can devise stronger ways to destroy them. Their escape is difficult because the great dome's opening and every other entrance are guarded, and there is no night to conceal their movement.
The prisoners survive Zog's attempt to crush them with marble blocks. Aquareine expects him to plan more powerful attacks and doubts that she will always be able to foil his magic.
Sacho says Zog has no time for vengeance, although he believes the magician may be plotting to kill the prisoners. He considers vengeance wrong and hopes the prisoners will escape it.

Magic causes the constant light in the castle and makes the castle invisible to those in the ocean unless Zog permits them to see it. Zog is said to possess clever magic that may make his attacks harder to resist.

l: day and night, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 16._
s: There is no day and night in the castle: it never becomes dark, and the light remains constant. The inhabitants sleep whenever they become tired and rise when rested.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 17._
s: Trot, Cap'n Bill, Aquareine, and Clia endure another attack by Zog, who makes the water in their rooms dangerously hot. They discuss escaping Zog's castle, but Aquareine decides they need a weapon to overcome the guards and obtains a golden sword from the castle's goldsmiths. With Cap'n Bill's traded tools as payment, a goldsmith forges the sword, and Aquareine later charms it with fairy powers. The group returns to the Rose Chamber and goes to sleep while Aquareine prepares the weapon for their planned escape.

Trot feels the extreme heat caused by Zog's boiling water and remains awake after the danger passes. She suggests swimming back through the maze and tunnel, but Cap'n Bill points out that the sea devils would drive them back. She is delighted when the golden sword is made and asks whether they can begin their escape immediately.

Cap'n Bill complains about the heat and says he does not want to be par-boiled. He suggests using his jackknife as a weapon, but Aquareine says she needs a golden sword. He persuades the goldsmith Agga-Groo to make the sword by trading his compass, scissors, and other small possessions, including his jackknife.

Aquareine cools the water after Zog makes it dangerously hot and leads the discussion about escaping. She decides that a weapon is needed to overcome the guards and asks a goldsmith to forge a golden sword. After the sword is made, she plans to charm it with fairy powers and promises that the group will escape.

Clia suggests that the group should destroy Zog so they can leave freely. She explains that King Anko could not destroy Zog because he could not reach him, while Aquareine can potentially do so. She also urges Agga-Groo to make the golden sword secretly.

Zog makes the water in the group's rooms boiling hot and continues plotting ways to destroy them. He is angry because they escaped the Yell-Maker, falling stones, and hot water. His power has strengthened the guards, slaves, and sea devils, but he fears King Anko and does not usually leave his retreat.

Sacho tells the group that Zog's hot water was foolish and that both vengeance and fear are wasting time. He takes them to the goldsmiths' shop without asking Zog's permission, because his orders allow them liberty in the castle. He later warns them that Zog intends to stop them from living and advises them to be careful.
The sea devils guard the route to the open ocean and previously drove Trot and the others back into the tunnel. Cap'n Bill expects them to block the group's escape again.
Some slaves in Zog's castle are goldsmiths who have been taught to forge and work metal under water. They live under Zog's control, and their work includes making gold ornaments and furniture.

The goldsmiths work in a large underwater shop using electric furnaces that can soften or melt metal. Agga-Groo, their foreman, explains that he was brought to Zog's castle as a slave and makes beautiful gold objects despite hating his life there.

Zog's castle contains rooms, corridors, a goldsmiths' shop, and entrances guarded by powerful beings. The group is allowed to move through parts of it under Sacho's supervision, while Zog repeatedly attempts to destroy them.

l: the Rose Chamber, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 17._
s: The group returns to the Rose Chamber after visiting the goldsmiths' shop. Sacho warns them there about Zog's intentions, and they later sleep there while Aquareine charms the golden sword.

The goldsmiths' shop is a large underwater room filled with gold, ornaments, and curious electric furnaces. The furnaces glow intensely, turn nearby water into steam, and allow metal to be melted, forged, or molded.

The golden sword is forged by Agga-Groo from soft, pure gold and has a graceful shape, a slender keen blade, and an ornamental handle. It would not withstand hard use because its edge would nick and curl, but Aquareine intends to give it fairy powers so it can obey her commands and fight their opponents.

Gold is plentiful in the ocean, coming from gold-bearing rocks, golden nuggets, and sunken ships. Underwater gold is worked in Zog's castle using electric furnaces, but its purity makes it too soft for a durable sword.

l: escape from Zog's castle, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 17._
s: The group considers returning through the maze and tunnel to the open ocean, but the sea devils would likely force them back. Aquareine instead plans to use the charmed golden sword to overcome the guards and secure their escape.

l: forging the golden sword, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 17._
s: Agga-Groo initially refuses to forge the sword because he fears Zog, but Cap'n Bill's steel jackknife and other tools persuade him. The goldsmith quickly makes a yellow-gold sword, which Aquareine accepts before returning to the Rose Chamber.

l: The Sea Fairies, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 18._
s: Zog freezes the water in the castle, trapping Trot, Cap'n Bill, Queen Aquareine, and Princess Clia in ice. Queen Aquareine uses her fairy wand to melt the ice and free them, then restores Cap'n Bill's warmth. She decides they must escape Zog's castle and uses the enchanted golden sword to break a window. The group swims toward the opening in the vast dome, where Aquareine intends to attack the prince of the sea devils and escape into the ocean.

Trot awakens frozen inside the ice surrounding her and realizes that Zog has imprisoned them. Queen Aquareine frees her, and Trot helps warm Cap'n Bill before courageously following the queen toward the opening in the dome.

Cap'n Bill is found almost frozen stiff in his room after Zog freezes the water. Trot and Princess Clia rub him to revive him, and Queen Aquareine restores his warmth with her fairy wand; he then agrees to follow her escape plan.

Zog uses magic to freeze all the water in the room while the others sleep, imprisoning and endangering them. His cruel designs have become so dangerous that Queen Aquareine decides they must leave his castle.

Queen Aquareine melts the ice around herself, Trot, Princess Clia, and Cap'n Bill with her magic and frees them. She decides to escape Zog's castle, breaks its window with the golden sword, and leads the group toward the opening in the dome to confront the prince of the sea devils.

Princess Clia is trapped in the ice but is not affected by the cold because she is a fairy. After Queen Aquareine frees her, she helps Trot warm Cap'n Bill and follows the group toward the opening in the dome.

l: the prince of the sea devils, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 18._
s: The prince of the sea devils guards the opening in the roof of the vast dome. Queen Aquareine plans to attack and destroy him with the golden sword so the group can escape into the ocean.
The sea devils are enemies of the group. The passages out of the castle are guarded by scores of them, making the opening in the dome the preferred escape route.

Zog's castle contains the frozen rooms and gardens where Trot, Cap'n Bill, Queen Aquareine, and Princess Clia are imprisoned. The group escapes its interior through a shattered window into the surrounding dome.
The vast dome surrounds Zog's castle and gardens with clear water. Its roof is about half a mile above the castle and contains an opening guarded by the prince of the sea devils.
The ocean lies beyond the opening in the dome. The group hopes to reach its clear waters after getting past the prince of the sea devils.
The golden sword receives a fairy charm from Queen Aquareine. She uses it to shatter the castle window and plans to use it against the prince of the sea devils.
Queen Aquareine uses the fairy wand to melt the ice and free the imprisoned group. She also waves it over Cap'n Bill to restore his natural warmth.

l: opening in the dome, The Sea Fairies, [Illustration: _Chap. 18._
s: The opening in the dome is far above the castle and is guarded by the prince of the sea devils. Queen Aquareine leads the group toward it as their chosen route of escape.
